text:
Carla S.: heads up — nightly e2e perf gate failed for 1740 -> throughput dropped ~35% around commit 9f3b2c. p50 looks ok but sustained tail pressure killed the overall score. anyone on call? :eyes:
Ben R.: copying infra team, but quick Q — is this the new kvm image roll? saw a few kube node reboots in the window.
Dmitri K.: infra did a kernel patch yesterday afternoon, but rollout was gradual. i'll check node timelines against the test run.
Alice M.: can you paste the perf summary and the failing step? might be the kv-cache warmup doing weird eviction patterns under our new batching.
Carla S.: summary below (snippet):
```
E2E-PERF (nightly) — run id: nightly-2026-06-10-03
Target throughput baseline: 1200 qps
Observed steady-state: 780 qps (20m window)
p99 latency: 210ms -> baseline 95ms
Top culprit: model-server-4 CPU steal, many KV cache misses
Logs: /ci/artifacts/nightly/1740/logs.tar.gz
```
Ben R.: ok. first quick action: rerun the same job on a fresh infra pool (no kernel patch) to see if it's infra-sourced or code. Can someone kick a rerun with `NO_KERNEL_ROLL=true` tag?
Carla S.: @ci-bot rerun nightly-1740 with env NO_KERNEL_ROLL=true please
ci-bot: Rerun requested by Carla S. — job queued (jenkins/eng-e2e#4821). Estimated start: 2m.
Dmitri K.: i'm pulling node allocation for the failed run now. early look: 3/8 shards showed >50% context-switches during the window, matches kernel churn.
Ben R.: if rerun passes, we blame the infra rollout and can revert/hold. if it fails still, we bisect commit range 9f3b2c..a1d5e1 for model/runtime changes.
Carla S.: rerun started. provisioning on a control pool (no-kernel). tagging results in threads.
ci-bot: Rerun completed — status: partial-pass. Throughput improved to 1150 qps but one shard still shows p99 spikes (150ms). Artifacts: /ci/artifacts/nightly/1740/rerun-4821/
Alice M.: partial pass suggests mixed causes. one shard still high — could be a deployment mismatch or a config leak (KV cache size). can we run the failing shard isolated with `--trace-kvcache`?
Dmitri K.: will instrument that shard next. also proposing a quick bisect: run tests on commits [9f3b2c..a1d5e1] with the control infra to narrow down if latest runtime flags introduced regression.
Ben R.: agreed. Carla, can you open a bisect task and assign to eng-runtime for tomorrow? note: try to keep runs small (10 commits per batch) to save budget.
Carla S.: created task ENG-RUNTIME-783: "e2e throughput bisect — nightly 1740" and scheduled initial bisection job. linking logs in the task.
Alice M.: quick note — if anyone touches batching/kv eviction flags, ping in the PR and mention this thread. seems sensitive. :memo:
Ben R.: thanks all — followups in ENG-RUNTIME-783. if infra is guilty we revert the kernel rollout; if not, we proceed with bisect.
Carla S.: wrapping up here — will post bisect updates. thanks for the quick responses. :raised_hands:
